name: tanist

attributes.attribute: elected helper who took over when the king died
chosen for merit and strength rather than birth

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The tanist was a chosen helper to a Celtic king. The Irish form of the word is tandiste. Early writers say that Celtic leaders kept an elected helper called the tanist. The poet Edmund Spenser wrote that the Irish still elected their kings in the seventeenth century. They also chose a tanist. The tanist took over the rule when the king died. The tanist won the office by strength and merit. He did not have to be of the royal family. Some scholars see the role as both religious and political.

okr.objective: Record the tanist as the elected assistant leader in Celtic kingship.
key_results: Defines the tanist as the elected helper who assumed the rule
States that Spenser saw the office among the Irish in the seventeenth century
Notes the office rose by merit and strength, not by birth
